facts.statement: The genus Antineosteus was described by Lelièvre in 1984.
Antineosteus lived during the Early Devonian (Emsian) in the Anti-Atlas Mountains of Morocco and the Barrandian area of the Czech Republic.
facts.quote: Antineosteus is an extinct genus of homostiid arthrodire from the Emsian, Early Devonian Kess-Kess Mounds, in the eastern Anti-Atlas Mountains, Morocco, and the Barrandian area of the Czech Republic.

facts.statement: Antineosteus rufus is estimated to have exceeded 3 meters in length based on comparisons with plates from better-preserved related taxa.
facts.quote: A. rufus is estimated to exceed 3 m, from measuring the plates with the ones from better-preserved, related taxa.

facts.statement: Antineosteus likely had a planktivorous or suspension-feeding lifestyle, supported by its large size and lack of bladed jaw teeth, similar to modern baleen whales or whale sharks.
facts.quote: Antineosteus, like many other members of Homostiidae, lacked bladed dentition on their jaws, and was large in size. These traits all in one animal support a planktivorous lifestyle, like baleen whales, or the whale shark, as supported by Denison, 1978, suggesting similar lifestyles for arthrodires like Homostius, making it reasonable for many homostiids to be suspension-feeders like the later Titanichthys.

facts.statement: Antineosteus is classified as a homostiid and is most closely related to the genus Homostius.
facts.quote: Antineosteus is a homostiid, closest related to Homostius.

facts.statement: Antineosteus belongs to the family Homostiidae within the class Placodermi.
Fossils of Antineosteus date from the Pragian to the Emsian stages, between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pragian to Emsian (413.02 to 393.47 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species Antineosteus lehmani is known only from fragmentary fossils including a left anterior dorsolateral plate, a left paranuchal plate, and an inferognathal.
rejected.quote: Antineosteus lehmani is rather fragmentary, known from a left anterior dorsolateral plate, a left paranuchal plate, and an inferognathal.
